item.title: Holiday Tips, Special Collections, and Food Waste Updates
item.description:
Thank you for continuing to help reduce wasted food! We have some updates about your efforts, some exciting news, and additional options to ensure food does not end up in our landfill.

We are pleased to share that your efforts to drop off food scraps at the Columbus Division of Refuse Collection's nine locations across the city have resulted in a total of 282,053 pounds of food composted as of September 2025. This is greater  than the weight of a blue whale! Keep up the good work by ensuring your food scraps do not contain any plastic bags, utensils, or wrappers. 

The City of Columbus, along with community including Columbus Food Rescue, were awarded a Special Mention for Food Waste at the recent Milan Urban Food Policy Pact Global Forum. The Department of Public Service and Columbus Public Health were recognized for efforts to educate residents, launch food scraps drop-off locations, and diverting food from the landfill through community efforts. 

Please don’t throw away pumpkins in your trash or recycling containers or at the city’s food scraps drop-off locations. Instead, toss them in your backyard or bring them to one of the Columbus Refuse Collection’s free pumpkin drop-off sites through the end of November. The Waste and Reuse Convenience Centers and the Stephen R. Lennon Refuse Collection Station will be accepting pumpkins and gourds for composting. 

Intact, decaying and carved pumpkins and gourds will be accepted. No trash, food, recycling or other waste should be included with the pumpkins. Remove candles, and do not include pumpkins that have been painted or drawn on with permanent markers.

Frying a turkey for Thanksgiving? The city's Waste and Reuse Convenience Centers now accept used cooking oil, fats, and grease. There are a few important things to know for acceptable drop-off:

  • Accepted: Used cooking oil, fats, and grease
  • Not Accepted: No petroleum products, motor oil, gasoline, diesel, or any other non-edible fats
  • Small bits of food such as crumbs from frying, are acceptable but large pieces should go in the food scraps drop-off bins

Columbus Blessing Boxes are provide a network of free little pantries spread across our community to provide food. These are a thoughtful and convenient way to donate and distribute non-perishable food items while preventing waste and unnecessary landfilling. The Blessing Boxes help to ensure that food is being used to the highest and best value. Feeding people and not landfills is a goal of our food waste work. Learn more and find your nearest Columbus Blessing Box here. 

Want to help even more? Invite friends, family, and neighbors to join the movement! Visit columbus.gov/foodwaste to learn more and to find the nearest food scraps drop-off location and learn more.

item.title: Thanks for Fighting Food Waste with Us! 🌍🥕
item.description:
Happy Food Waste Prevention Week! 🎉

On behalf of the City of Columbus, I want to extend a heartfelt thank you for being part of our Food Scraps Drop-Off program. Because of your efforts (and those of your neighbors), we’ve diverted more than 185,919 pounds of food scraps from the landfill since launching the program — that’s nearly 94 tons of waste that’s now being composted instead of contributing to greenhouse gas emissions.

This impact is critical to reaching the City’s Climate Action Plan goal of becoming carbon neutral by 2050 — and you’re helping lead the way. 🌱♻️

Here are a few more easy ways to keep reducing food waste at home:

🛒 Rescue edible food – Learn how you can support or volunteer with Columbus Food Rescue, which redistributes excess food to those in need.

📦 Understand date labels – “Best by” and “sell by” dates usually refer to quality, not safety. When in doubt, trust your senses.

🥶 Store food properly – Keep your fridge at 40°F or below, freeze leftovers, and store herbs like fresh flowers in a glass of water.

📢 Want to help even more? Invite friends, family, or neighbors to join the movement! Visit columbus.gov/foodwaste to find the nearest food scraps drop-off location and learn more.

Together, we’re building a cleaner, greener, and more sustainable Columbus. Thank you again for doing your part!
